# When Americans choose Chinese AI

Rest of World, by Viola Zhou, June 17, 2026. Full article retrieved.

## Key findings
- **Stu Clott** (San Diego ops manager/part-time developer): an hour of coding costs ~$10 on Claude but <50 cents on DeepSeek. "The output quality, to be honest, I can't tell the difference."
- **Microsoft** is exploring DeepSeek (or another open-source model) as a lower-cost alternative for Copilot Cowork, currently powered by Anthropic and OpenAI systems (per Axios, June 16, 2026).
- Chinese companies keep prices low via lower domestic salaries/infrastructure costs, open models, and subsidized plans. DeepSeek, Xiaomi MiMo, and Minimax rank among the most cost-efficient on the Artificial Analysis cost-vs-intelligence index.
- **Lindy** (SF, AI work assistants): founder Flo Crivello switched from Anthropic to DeepSeek (announced on X in June 2026); saved the firm "millions of dollars." "You don't need God to write your email... If you can get those lower tiers of intelligence for a tenth of the price, it would be foolish not to do it."
- **Ruben Garcia Jr.** (Dallas developer): pays $500/mo for Claude + ChatGPT (complex planning/review) and $200/mo for Minimax, Moonshot Kimi, and Xiaomi MiMo, which "handle 90% of the tasks" (coding, voice recognition).
- **OpenRouter**: DeepSeek, Tencent, Minimax, and Xiaomi models are now the four most popular.
- **Vercel**: DeepSeek's share of token usage jumped from under 1% to 17% in May, while its share of revenue stayed near 1%.
- **Kyle Chan** (Brookings fellow): "[AI] adoption at large companies is fairly saturated. The growth market for Chinese companies would be medium-sized businesses that are starting to get into AI but are wary of the costs."
- **Political scrutiny**: House lawmakers launched investigations into Airbnb and Anysphere (Cursor) after they disclosed using Chinese open models (Qwen, Kimi) for AI infrastructure. Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky clarified the company was not sending data to the model developers.
- **Poe Zhao** (Hello China Tech, Beijing): large/regulated firms will be reluctant due to data security, censorship, and geopolitical risk. Some US businesses run open-source models on their own servers or access them via American cloud providers; Lindy accessed DeepSeek through an American provider. "Chinese models are becoming part of the global AI infrastructure layer. But usage is only the first step. The next test is whether Chinese model developers can convert that usage into revenue, enterprise trust, and durable distribution."
- OpenAI is considering significant price cuts as it competes with Anthropic for enterprise users (per WSJ).
